pack.description: Vocabulary of environmental science passages and talks: climate, pollution, resources and conservation.
pack.selection_note: Internal selection of terms that recur in introductory environmental science texts; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: gas or other matter that is sent out into the air, or the act of sending it out
entries.example_academic: Emissions from transport have risen even as those from industry have fallen.
entries.example_spoken: The new buses produce almost no emissions.

entries.definition: describing energy or materials that come from sources that nature replaces and that do not run out
entries.example_academic: Renewable sources now supply more than a third of the region's electricity.
entries.example_spoken: The campus runs mostly on renewable energy.

entries.definition: a gas in the air, such as carbon dioxide or methane, that traps heat near the surface of the planet
entries.example_academic: Methane is a more powerful greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide over short periods.
entries.example_spoken: Cows produce a surprising amount of greenhouse gas.

entries.definition: the cutting down of the trees over a large area
entries.example_academic: Deforestation reduces rainfall in regions far from the cleared land.
entries.example_spoken: Palm oil is one of the main causes of deforestation.

entries.definition: a substance that makes air, water or soil dirty or harmful
entries.example_academic: The filter removes most pollutants before the water returns to the river.
entries.example_spoken: Fine dust is the pollutant doctors worry about most.

entries.definition: able to continue for a long time without damaging the environment or using up resources
entries.example_academic: Sustainable fishing limits the catch to what the population can replace.
entries.example_spoken: That pace of work isn't sustainable for a whole semester.

entries.definition: the total amount of carbon dioxide released by the activities of a person, company or product
entries.example_academic: The study compared the carbon footprint of locally grown and imported vegetables.
entries.example_spoken: I'm trying to shrink my carbon footprint by flying less.

entries.definition: a fuel such as coal, oil or gas that was formed underground from dead plants and animals over millions of years
entries.example_academic: Burning fossil fuels returns carbon to the atmosphere that was stored for millions of years.
entries.example_spoken: The city wants to stop heating buildings with fossil fuels.

entries.definition: a long period with little or no rain
entries.example_academic: A decade of drought forced farmers to abandon the northern plains.
entries.example_spoken: We're not allowed to water the lawn during the drought.

entries.definition: the protection of nature, or the careful use of a resource so that it is not wasted
entries.example_academic: Conservation efforts have concentrated on areas with the greatest variety of species.
entries.example_spoken: She volunteers for a bird conservation group.

entries.definition: to make something dirty or dangerous by adding a harmful substance
entries.example_academic: Leaking tanks contaminated the groundwater beneath the factory.
entries.example_spoken: Don't use that spoon; you'll contaminate the sample.

entries.definition: able to be broken down naturally by bacteria into harmless substances
entries.example_academic: Biodegradable packaging decomposes within months under the right conditions.
entries.example_spoken: These cups are biodegradable, so put them in the green bin.

entries.definition: a place where waste is buried under the ground
entries.example_academic: Organic waste in landfills generates methane as it decays.
entries.example_spoken: Most of that plastic ends up in a landfill.

entries.definition: rain or other liquid that flows over the land into rivers and lakes, often carrying chemicals
entries.example_academic: Agricultural runoff carries fertilizer into rivers and coastal waters.
entries.example_spoken: The runoff from the parking lot goes straight into the creek.

entries.definition: a large reduction in the amount of something, so that not enough is left
entries.example_academic: The depletion of groundwater threatens agriculture across the region.
entries.example_spoken: Overfishing led to the depletion of cod stocks.

entries.definition: a layer of gas high above the Earth that stops much of the sun's harmful radiation from reaching the surface
entries.example_academic: The ozone layer has begun to recover since the damaging chemicals were banned.
entries.example_spoken: Those old spray cans were bad for the ozone layer.

entries.definition: the process of capturing a gas, especially carbon dioxide, and storing it so that it does not enter the air
entries.example_academic: Forests contribute to carbon sequestration by storing carbon in wood and soil.
entries.example_spoken: The company claims sequestration will cancel out its pollution.

entries.definition: the process by which fertile land turns into dry land where little can grow
entries.example_academic: Overgrazing accelerates desertification along the southern edge of the grasslands.
entries.example_spoken: Planting trees is one way to slow desertification.

entries.definition: the process in which too many nutrients enter a lake or river, causing plants to grow fast and use up the oxygen
entries.example_academic: Eutrophication produced a layer of algae that blocked sunlight from the lake bed.
entries.example_spoken: The green water is a sign of eutrophication.

entries.definition: a layer of rock or sand under the ground that holds water
entries.example_academic: The aquifer is being pumped faster than rainfall can refill it.
entries.example_spoken: The whole town gets its water from one aquifer.

entries.definition: ground that stays frozen all year round
entries.example_academic: Thawing permafrost releases gases that have been trapped for millennia.
entries.example_spoken: You can't dig foundations easily in permafrost.

entries.definition: caused by human activity
entries.example_academic: Anthropogenic warming is now detectable in ocean temperatures at great depth.
entries.example_spoken: The report separates natural causes from anthropogenic ones.

entries.definition: the process of becoming more acid
entries.example_academic: Ocean acidification weakens the shells of many marine organisms.
entries.example_spoken: Acidification is bad news for oyster farms.

entries.definition: the amount of salt that is contained in water or soil
entries.example_academic: Rising salinity has made much of the irrigated land unproductive.
entries.example_spoken: They check the salinity of the pool every morning.

entries.definition: liquid waste that flows out of a factory or sewage system into a river or the sea
entries.example_academic: Untreated effluent from the mill killed fish for several kilometers downstream.
entries.example_spoken: The plant was fined for dumping effluent into the bay.

entries.definition: plant or animal material used as fuel, or the total mass of living things in an area
entries.example_academic: Biomass can be burned directly or converted into liquid fuel.
entries.example_spoken: The heating plant on campus burns biomass, mostly wood chips.

entries.definition: an area of land from which all the water flows into the same river or lake; also, a turning point
entries.example_academic: Protecting the watershed is cheaper than building a new treatment plant.
entries.example_spoken: The election was a watershed for the country.

entries.definition: the moment when a series of small changes becomes large enough to cause a bigger change that is hard to stop
entries.example_academic: Beyond a certain tipping point, the ice sheet would continue to melt even if warming stopped.
entries.example_spoken: We reached a tipping point when half the class had dropped out.

entries.definition: to pass slowly out of soil or another material into water, or to remove a substance in this way
entries.example_academic: Heavy rain leaches nitrates from the fields into nearby streams.
entries.example_spoken: Chemicals from the old dump are leaching into the well.
